title: Changing editor camera by code makes it unresponsive to user
body:
### Tested versions

v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-1620 v4 @ 3.50GHz (8 threads) - 63.91 GiB memory

### Issue description

Hi,

I'm working on a small VR project, where most of the experience is looking at things from a slowly moving vehicle. The first prototype actually had the world moving backward while the vehicle stays at origin. It was great for iterating because it allowed to move the viewport camera around while the animation is playing (mimicking the actual in-game experience). But the vehicle trajectory became a bit more complex and we changed to actually moving the vehicle within the fixed world.

I've then made a simple plugin to have the viewport camera locked on an object, i.e. it wouldn't move relatively to the object, whether the object moves or not. Nothing fancy, just matrix manipulations.

When the object doesn't move, the camera reacts to user inputs as usual (moving, zooming, orbiting...).

When the object moves, the camera moves as well as designed, but **doesn't react to user inputs anymore**.

My guess is that it conflicts with camera smoothing magics. But I'm not able to dig into the code. Looking at https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115957, I've seen code to check whether camera transform is "equal" when the change is lower than epsilon. There's also the concept of Cursor, which especially makes sense for orbiting, but it isn't exposed to GDScript.

Or, could a C++ module achieve that?

I'd release the plugin anyway, although it's a bit frustrating right now. Unless you decide to get this feature into the core.

Thanks!

### Steps to reproduce

Not reproducing the matrix thing: it's enough to move the camera to get it unresponsive to user inputs.
 
- Create a node with the following code.
- Notice the viewport camera does not react anymore to user inputs.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

```gdscript
@tool
extends Node3D

func _process(_delta):
	var camera = EditorInterface.get_editor_viewport_3d(0).get_camera_3d()
	camera.transform.origin.z -= 0.00001  # play with this
```
